hypothesis: A 12-call discovery cap with the receipt-bound terminal shortlist preserves or improves final source selection while materially reducing model tokens and wall time versus the native convergence baseline.
decision_rule: Run and report both tasks with sealed predictions before pinned native scoring. For each task candidate Span-F1 and File-F1 must strictly exceed control; known model tokens and measured wall duration must both be strictly lower. Both tasks must pass all four gates for a replicated quality-and-efficiency claim. An unscored arm is inconclusive. No candidate changes after the first dispatch.
gold_posture: Task choice used only source-only task statements and cached repository availability. Exact task gold and prior predictions were not inspected before freeze; these instance IDs were not referenced by existing benchmark evidence.
claim_ceiling: A two-task G01 cross-repository replication, not the complete ContextBench campaign or the full cross-benchmark ARE product goal.
open_questions: Does a hard 12-call cap leave enough evidence for accurate terminal selection on both new tasks?
How much of the measured duration improvement comes from fewer model requests versus local source-index work?
